key_insight: Latent surrogate solvers fail in long rollouts mainly because their representations are trained for reconstruction, not stable dynamics, so the latent space must be shaped for forecasting rather than compression alone.
engineering_relevance: For solid mechanics surrogates, training the latent space for rollout stability can cut compute and memory dramatically while preserving or improving long-horizon prediction on expensive time-dependent simulations.
method: Train latent spaces with Koopman operator learning to better support linearizable long-term dynamics.
Add Hamming noise during autoencoder training and noise injection during dynamics training to improve robustness.
Fine-tune with multi-step rollout objectives to reduce error accumulation over long horizons.
evidence_signal: Across two physics benchmarks and mesoscale crystal-plasticity fatigue simulations, these interventions reduced long-rollout error by about 40%, matched or exceeded full-resolution accuracy, and used roughly 100x fewer FLOPs and half the GPU memory.
watch_item: Methods that improve rollout stability can hurt reconstruction and one-step accuracy, so implementation must balance standard training metrics against long-horizon performance.
paper_title: Beyond Compression: Training Latent Representations for Stable Long-Horizon Rollout in Neural Surrogate Solvers
